notes: Data came from the Next.js App Router RSC flight payload embedded in the leaderboard document (self.__next_f), not from a separate XHR/fetch endpoint, same as the 20260902/20260903 scrapes. Script tags containing `self.__next_f.push(...)` were read from document.querySelectorAll('script') and evaluated with a stubbed push() to capture the (id, stringChunk) pairs.

The combined flight text again contains TWO top-level "models":[ arrays (a slim model-picker list and the full leaderboard payload). This scrape took the LAST occurrence (offset ~283.9k chars into a ~3.16M char flight text), which is the full 94-field payload; the first occurrence (offset ~10.6k chars) is the lightweight picker list, consistent with the 20260903 finding.

raw.json is the verbatim `models` array (last occurrence) from that payload, 643 model entries, ~2.85 MB, extracted via balanced-bracket text slicing (not regex) and JSON.parse'd in-browser via evaluate_script with filePath, saved directly to disk.

Unlike the 20260902/20260903 notes, this snapshot's flight text did NOT contain the literal "$undefined" sentinel string anywhere (verified by substring search on the full raw text); missing fields serialize as JSON null in today's payload instead. Both null and (defensively) the literal string "$undefined" are treated as absent when building normalized.json, so behavior is unchanged even though the sentinel form apparently changed server-side.
Benchmark and metric display names are the same mapping used on 20260903; every record keeps the exact original payload key in `source_field`.

DEEPER THAN REFERENCE: the raw payload also exposes 8 scalar Intelligence-Index evaluation-cost/time fields (intelligenceIndexCostInput, intelligenceIndexCostOutput, intelligenceIndexCostReasoning, intelligenceIndexCostAnswer, intelligenceIndexCostTotal, intelligenceIndexCostPerTask, intelligenceIndexOutputTokensPerTask, intelligenceIndexTimePerTask) that were present with real values in the 20260903 raw.json too but were never added to metrics_captured. This scrape adds them as new metric rows (intelligence_index_cost_*_usd, intelligence_index_output_tokens_per_task, intelligence_index_time_per_task_seconds) per the instruction to capture every metric the payload exposes, not just what the reference chose to keep. They are populated for 178-191 of the 643 models (models without a reported Intelligence Index, or without cost breakdown data, have them null/absent).

NOT flattened into normalized.json (left as unexploited depth, noted here rather than invented): gdpvalBreakdown, multilingualBreakdown, opennessBreakdown, omniscienceBreakdown, evalTokenCounts and intelligenceIndexTokenCounts are all nested objects (per-category sub-scores / per-eval token counts), not single scalars, so they don't fit the flat (model, benchmark/metric, score) row schema without a schema change. A future scrape could explode these into their own sub-benchmark rows if desired.
`rank` is present only on Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index records and is derived by sorting all 630 models that report a non-null index descending; it is not a rank published by the site.
`cost_usd` on every record is the model-level blended price per 1M tokens at a 3:1 input:output ratio (field price1mBlended0To3To1), attached as cost context; it is not a per-benchmark cost.
`date` is the model release date (releaseDate) reported by the site, not the scrape date.
Score scales are as published: eval scores are fractions 0-1 (e.g. gpqa), index values are on their own scales. No rescaling applied.
Null values were omitted rather than filled (no live "$undefined" sentinel was observed this run; see note above).
changes_vs_20260903: model_count 636 -> 643 (net +7 model/effort entries in the leaderboard payload); row_count 17254 -> 18834 (the row_count jump is larger than the model_count delta because this scrape also adds 8 new Intelligence-Index cost/time metric columns across ~180-190 models, on top of the normal per-model growth).
Models with a reported (non-null) Intelligence Index: 623 -> 630.

Checked models: Muse Spark 1.3 present with (max) and (xhigh) effort variants (same two as 20260903; xhigh has full price/speed data, max still has price/speed absent -- only its Intelligence Index score is populated). Gemini 3.8 Flash present with (low), (medium), (high) effort variants, all three fully populated. Grok 4.6 (xhigh) present and fully populated. GLM-5.3-Flash was already present on 20260903 (not new) and remains fully populated.

Model roster diff vs 20260903: 9 names added, 2 removed (net +7). Added: GPT-6 Astra in six variants (low/medium/high/xhigh/max/Non-reasoning), K2 Horizon 375B A23B, and two renamed/re-labeled entries that look like the same underlying models reappearing with a fuller variant label -- 'HyperNova 60B 2605' -> 'HyperNova 60B 2605 (high, based on gpt-oss-120b)' and 'Quasar 438B' -> 'Quasar 438B (max, based on GLM-5.2)'. Removed (by exact name match): the old unlabeled 'HyperNova 60B 2605' and 'Quasar 438B' entries superseded by the relabeled ones above.

Schema field `cweBench` (present as a key on all records in 20260902/20260903, but $undefined/valueless on every one) has DISAPPEARED entirely from the per-model object schema in today's payload -- it is not just null, the key itself is gone. Raw key count per model went 95 -> 94.

The RSC serialization sentinel changed: 20260902/20260903 payloads used the literal string "$undefined" for missing fields; today's payload uses JSON null instead. No functional impact on normalized.json (both treated as absent) but noted as a drift in how the site serializes missing data.
No other fields disappeared from the 20260903 metrics/benchmarks schema; MMLU-Pro, AIME and LiveCodeBench are still not present in this payload.

No page failures once the correct page/tab was captured; extraction script itself ran cleanly. Note for future runs: this browser session had 9 other agents scraping concurrently and the shared 'selected page' pointer was being changed by other agents on almost every single tool call -- roughly 60 consecutive select_page+evaluate_script attempts landed on another agent's page before one finally hit this page's URL. This was pure MCP-session contention, not a site-side issue; once raw.json was captured, all normalization/meta work was done locally without touching the browser again.
